type.label: Weakness of long finger extensor muscles

phenotypicFeatures.description: gradually progressive difficulty extending his fingers
Distal predominant muscle weakness was noted, most prominent in the bilateral index finger and left fourth and fifth finger extensors where differential weakness was seen (MRC grade 1–2
Mild muscle weakness was noted in axial muscles (neck flexion MRC grade 3, neck extension 4)

needle electromyography (EMG) revealed myopathic changes as characterized by low amplitude, short duration, polyphasic motor unit potentials with early recruitment, increased insertion activities without fibrillation potentials or positive sharp waves
fatty infiltration in gluteus maximus/ medius, sartorius, adductor magnus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris, extensor digitorum longus, tibialis anterior, and soleus

type.label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter

phenotypicFeatures.description: Scattered and clustered predominantly atrophic type 2 fibres, together with nuclear clumps were seen
Focal areas of endomysial and perimysial fibrosis, and increased adipose tissue were noted

type.label: Abnormal muscle tissue enzyme activity or level

phenotypicFeatures.description: Some fibres showed pale central areas on NADH (Fig. C) and SDH stains (Fig. F) but not on COX stain (Fig. E), suggesting regions with reduced oxidative enzyme activities
